Based on the volumes provided, we can determine the dimensions of the constituent blocks.

1.  **Identify Dimensions of the Cube:**
    The gray block is a cube with volume $125 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$.
    Side length of the cube $= \sqrt[3]{125} = 5 \mathrm{~cm}$.

2.  **Identify Dimensions of the Smaller Rectangular Block:**
    The problem states the smaller rectangular block has volume $75 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$. From the diagram, this block is joined to the cube. For them to form a single larger rectangular block, they must share a face. The shared face is the vertical side of the cube, which has dimensions $5 \mathrm{~cm} \times 5 \mathrm{~cm}$. Therefore, the base of the smaller block is $5 \mathrm{~cm} \times 5 \mathrm{~cm}$, and its height is the same as the cube's height, $5 \mathrm{~cm}$.
    Volume $= \text{base area} \times \text{height} \Rightarrow 75 = (5 \times 5) \times h$.
    $75 = 25h$
    $h = 3 \mathrm{~cm}$.
    So, the smaller block has dimensions $5 \times 5 \times 3 \mathrm{~cm}$.

3.  **Identify Dimensions of the Remaining Block:**
    The total volume of the large block is $280 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$.
    Volume of the third block $= \text{Total Volume} - (\text{Volume of Cube} + \text{Volume of Small Block})$.
    Volume $= 280 - (125 + 75) = 280 - 200 = 80 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$.
    Looking at the diagram, this third block forms the back layer of the assembly. It shares the same width ($5 \mathrm{~cm}$) and height ($5 \mathrm{~cm}$) as the front layer.
    $80 = 5 \times 5 \times d$
    $80 = 25d$
    $d = 3.2 \mathrm{~cm}$.

4.  **Calculate the Area of the Question Mark Face:**
    The face marked with the question mark is the top face of the back block.
    Its dimensions are the width of the block ($5 \mathrm{~cm}$) and the depth of the back block ($3.2 \mathrm{~cm}$).
    Area $= 5 \mathrm{~cm} \times 3.2 \mathrm{~cm} = 16 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$.

A: $16 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
